chunks: And it is narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar that he said:

When a man from the Banu al-Abbas comes to power, named Abdullah, who is 'the one with the eye' (the prominent one), they begin with him and end with him. He is the key to calamity and the sword of annihilation. When a letter is read to him in Syria from 'Abdullah, Abdullah, Commander of the Faithful', you will not long before you hear that a letter has been read on the pulpit of Egypt: 'From Abdullah, Abd al-Rahman, Commander of the Faithful.' In another narration, he said: The rule will remain with the Banu al-Abbas until you receive a letter read in Egypt from 'Abdullah, Abd al-Rahman, Commander of the Faithful'. When that happens, it is the end of their rule and the termination of their duration. When the morning announcement is read for the Banu al-Abbas from 'Abdullah (Abdullah), Commander of the Faithful', wait for the evening announcement to be read to you from 'Abdullah, Abd al-Rahman, Commander of the Faithful'. And woe to Abdullah from Abd al-Rahman.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for the Caliph/Imam
key_terms.بَنُو الْعَبَّاسِ: Banu al-Abbas, the clan that established the Abbasid Caliphate
key_terms.عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ: Abd al-Rahman, the figure who succeeds or conflicts with Abdullah
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: Abdullah, a specific Caliph identified in the prophecy
key_terms.كَعْبُ الْأَحْبَارِ: Ka'b al-Ahbar, a prominent early Jewish convert to Islam known for his interpretations

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the decline of the Abbasid Caliphate according to Ka'b al-Ahbar?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites Ka'b al-Ahbar’s prophecy to identify a specific Caliph named Abdullah as the pivotal figure whose reign marks the beginning of the Abbasid decline, serving as a precursor to the end of their temporal rule. The narration details a symbolic transition where correspondence from 'Abdullah' in Syria is followed by 'Abd al-Rahman' in Egypt, signaling internal strife and the eventual 'woe' that accompanies the end of their dynasty's duration.
